changesets.summary: Compact ink for drawings that ship to a browser
changesets.details:
`skribble_rough` can write pen-shaped ink compactly: `CompactSvgInkOutline`, `InkStroke::compact_svg_path_data`, `DrawableInk::compact_svg_paths`, and `SketchOptions::tolerance`. The pen samples a stroke about every pen width, which keeps the taper smooth but writes far more points than a screen shows. Compact ink drops the samples within the tolerance of the line through their neighbours, draws through the rest with the same midpoint curves, and writes two decimals. The default output is unchanged, so ink still matches the Dart and TypeScript engines.

`skribble_core`'s `Scribble` draws compact ink within a quarter of a logical pixel. Its paths are about a sixth of the full size: a server-rendered page of sketches dropped from 1.2 MB to 370 KB.

changesets.summary: Smaller SVG path data for server-rendered sketches
changesets.details:
`compactSvgPath` rewrites SVG path data in its smallest equivalent form: relative commands, implicit command repeats, no leading zeros, and no separator where a minus sign or second decimal point already starts the next number. It rounds absolute coordinates to the precision you ask for (one decimal by default) and writes the deltas in whole units of that precision, so a long path never drifts. Every path command is understood, including arcs with packed flags; data it cannot parse comes back unchanged.

`RoughSvg.compact()` applies it to all three groups. At its default of two decimals it draws exactly the shape `RoughSvg.fromDrawable` writes, in about a fifth fewer bytes.

`skribble_jaspr` components now write compact path data in every ink overlay, with no change to what they draw.

changesets.summary: Keep rough icon font lookups constant

`flutter build web --release` rejects an app that depends on `skribble_icons_material` (including through `skribble_icons`) because `lookupMaterialRoughIconsIconData` constructed `IconData` from a code point read at runtime. Icon tree-shaking requires every `IconData` it can see to be a constant, and it aborts rather than guessing which glyphs to keep.

The generator now emits `kMaterialRoughIconsByIdentifier`, a const map of `IconData`, and the lookup indexes that map. Apps that register the Material catalog still ship the whole rough icon font, because a const map keeps every entry alive. Named `static const` fields would let unused glyphs drop out, and that remains a follow-up. changesets.summary: skribble_core: skribble's design system for Rust, free of any UI framework
changesets.details:
The Rust crates no longer build leptoskit components. `skribble_leptoskit`, `skribble_leptoskit_charts`, and `skribble_leptoskit_maps` are gone from this repository, and their framework-free parts now live in one new crate, `skribble_core`, which depends on nothing but `skribble_rough`. leptoskit changes faster than skribble can track, so the leptoskit components move into the leptoskit repository as `leptoskit_skribble`, built on `skribble_core`, where they can follow leptoskit's own API.

`skribble_core` holds:

- **Colours.** The `colorway` module: `Rgba`, the named `swatch`es (Flutter's `WiredPalette` values), `Appearance`, the sunny, berry, ocean, citrus, and quiet `Colorway`s, WCAG contrast, and the default 1.6-pixel pen at playful roughness. `Theme` and `Palette` build on it: `Theme::SKRIBBLE` is the sunny colourway, `Theme::colorway` picks another, and `marker()`, `accent()`, `accent_at(i)`, and `on(wash)` match the Flutter theme.
- **Component ink.** The `components` module has a recipe for every component the leptoskit crate drew: `button`, `boxed`, `card`, `circle`, `badge`, `input`, `divider`, `checkbox`, `radio`, `switch`, `progress`, and `highlight`. Each returns an `Ink` (a shape, its outline, and its fill) whose drawing stretches to the component behind it, plus the tone that reads on its fill.
- **Scribbles.** `Scribble` draws arrows, curves, and annotations at an explicit size with the pen's compact, tapered ink, and returns an error instead of panicking for a bad size or shape.
- **Charts.** `charts::CandlestickChart`, `LineChart`, and `BarChart` draw at an explicit size with exact price geometry, and return an error for a size that is not positive and finite. `ChartTheme`, `indicators`, and `geometry` move unchanged.
- **Maps.** `maps::Camera`, `LatLng`, `LatLngBounds`, `MapFeature`, `MapStyle`, and `PinCategory` move unchanged, with `features_drawing`, `graticule`, `pin_drawing`, `pin_origin`, `zoom_button_drawing`, and `zoom_steps` for the ink the leptoskit map drew.

Every drawing is an `InkDrawing`: SVG path data with a light and a dark `Tone` per path. `runs()` groups paths by tone for renderers that recolour ink through a text colour, and `to_svg(appearance)` writes a standalone SVG document.

The workspace no longer depends on leptoskit or leptos, so it drops its `[patch.crates-io]` pin of leptoskit `main`. The docs replace the three leptoskit guides with [skribble for Rust](https://openbudgetfun.github.io/skribble/docs/guides/rust) and a short note on moving to `leptoskit_skribble`.

#### Shrink long labels to fit on one line

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #286](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/skribble/pull/286)

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #281](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/skribble/pull/281) · _Closed issues:_ [#198](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/skribble/issues/198)

`flutter build web --release` rejects an app that depends on `skribble_icons_material` (including through `skribble_icons`) because `lookupMaterialRoughIconsIconData` constructed `IconData` from a code point read at runtime. Icon tree-shaking requires every `IconData` it can see to be a constant, and it aborts rather than guessing which glyphs to keep.

The generator now emits `kMaterialRoughIconsByIdentifier`, a const map of `IconData`, and the lookup indexes that map. Apps that register the Material catalog still ship the whole rough icon font, because a const map keeps every entry alive. Named `static const` fields would let unused glyphs drop out, and that remains a follow-up. The storybook icon gallery still builds `IconData` from a runtime code point on purpose, so its web release build keeps `--no-tree-shake-icons`.

entries:
#### Vivid colourways and lively motion by default

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #283](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/skribble/pull/283)

skribble now looks like a sticker book out of the box instead of a pencil sketch on grey paper, and the docs and agent instructions steer people and coding agents toward colour and motion rather than safe, muted designs.

**Colour.** `WiredColorway` (`sunny`, `berry`, `ocean`, `citrus`, and the calm `quiet`) and `WiredThemeData.colorway(...)` build light and dark themes from a set of vivid washes added to `WiredPalette` (`sunshine`, `tomato`, `tangerine`, `sky`, `aqua`, `mint`, `lime`, `bubblegum`, `grape`, `cobalt`, `cherry`, `cherryGlow`). Every wash keeps 4.5:1 contrast with plum ink and night text. `WiredThemeData` gains `accentColor` and `accents`, with `accentAt(index)` for colour-coding content, and `onColor`, `onMarkerColor`, `onAccentColor`, and `inkOn` for labels on a wash. `cuddly()` is the sunny colourway.

The defaults change: the marker is `sunshine` (was `lilac`), errors use `cherry`, `WiredFilledButton`, `WiredFloatingActionButton`, and `WiredBadge` fill with the accent (tomato), and selected choice and filter chips are coloured in with the marker instead of solid ink. Selected navigation, segmented, toggle, and stepper items use `onMarkerColor`. Pass `WiredThemeData.colorway(WiredColorway.quiet)` to keep the earlier lilac look. `WiredCard` takes a `color` and inks its content to match. The Material bridge maps `accentColor` to and from `ColorScheme.tertiary`.

**Motion.** `WiredEntrance` springs a child in while its ink draws on, `WiredEntrance.staggered` and `WiredCascade` bring lists and columns in one after another, `WiredBoil` gives focal drawings the wriggle of hand-drawn animation, `WiredHighlight` swipes a marker or underline behind words, and `WiredCurves` (`springy`, `snappy`, `bouncy`, `pen`) and `WiredSpringCurve` time your own animations. All of it settles at once when `WiredMotion` is off or the platform asks for reduced motion.

**Web.** `skribble_jaspr`'s stylesheet uses the sunny colours, adds `--skribble-marker`, `--skribble-on-marker`, and six `--skribble-wash-*` properties with matching `skribble-wash-1` to `skribble-wash-6` classes, and adds the `skribble-draw`, `skribble-pop`, and `skribble-lift` motion classes, all behind `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`. Stroked paths carry `pathLength="1"` so they can draw on.

The new [Vivid and alive](https://openbudgetfun.github.io/skribble/guides/vivid-design) guide holds the design rules, shared with `AGENTS.md` and the agents reference page.

#### Smaller SVG path data for server-rendered sketches

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #290](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/skribble/pull/290)

`compactSvgPath` rewrites SVG path data in its smallest equivalent form: relative commands, implicit command repeats, no leading zeros, and no separator where a minus sign or second decimal point already starts the next number. It rounds absolute coordinates to the precision you ask for (one decimal by default) and writes the deltas in whole units of that precision, so a long path never drifts. Every path command is understood, including arcs with packed flags; data it cannot parse comes back unchanged.

`RoughSvg.compact()` applies it to all three groups. At its default of two decimals it draws exactly the shape `RoughSvg.fromDrawable` writes, in about a fifth fewer bytes.

`skribble_jaspr` components now write compact path data in every ink overlay, with no change to what they draw.

#### Compact ink for drawings that ship to a browser

_Packages:_ 🟠 _rust:skribble_rough_

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #278](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/skribble/pull/278)

`skribble_rough` can write pen-shaped ink compactly: `CompactSvgInkOutline`, `InkStroke::compact_svg_path_data`, `DrawableInk::compact_svg_paths`, and `SketchOptions::tolerance`. The pen samples a stroke about every pen width, which keeps the taper smooth but writes far more points than a screen shows. Compact ink drops the samples within the tolerance of the line through their neighbours, draws through the rest with the same midpoint curves, and writes two decimals. The default output is unchanged, so ink still matches the Dart and TypeScript engines.

`skribble_core`'s `Scribble` draws compact ink within a quarter of a logical pixel. Its paths are about a sixth of the full size: a server-rendered page of sketches dropped from 1.2 MB to 370 KB.

#### skribble_core: skribble's design system for Rust, free of any UI framework

_Packages:_ 🟠 _skribble_core_

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #287](https://github.com/openbudgetfun/skribble/pull/287)

The Rust crates no longer build leptoskit components. `skribble_leptoskit`, `skribble_leptoskit_charts`, and `skribble_leptoskit_maps` are gone from this repository, and their framework-free parts now live in one new crate, `skribble_core`, which depends on nothing but `skribble_rough`. leptoskit changes faster than skribble can track, so the leptoskit components move into the leptoskit repository as `leptoskit_skribble`, built on `skribble_core`, where they can follow leptoskit's own API.

`skribble_core` holds:

- **Colours.** The `colorway` module: `Rgba`, the named `swatch`es (Flutter's `WiredPalette` values), `Appearance`, the sunny, berry, ocean, citrus, and quiet `Colorway`s, WCAG contrast, and the default 1.6-pixel pen at playful roughness. `Theme` and `Palette` build on it: `Theme::SKRIBBLE` is the sunny colourway, `Theme::colorway` picks another, and `marker()`, `accent()`, `accent_at(i)`, and `on(wash)` match the Flutter theme.
- **Component ink.** The `components` module has a recipe for every component the leptoskit crate drew: `button`, `boxed`, `card`, `circle`, `badge`, `input`, `divider`, `checkbox`, `radio`, `switch`, `progress`, and `highlight`. Each returns an `Ink` (a shape, its outline, and its fill) whose drawing stretches to the component behind it, plus the tone that reads on its fill.
- **Scribbles.** `Scribble` draws arrows, curves, and annotations at an explicit size with the pen's compact, tapered ink, and returns an error instead of panicking for a bad size or shape.
- **Charts.** `charts::CandlestickChart`, `LineChart`, and `BarChart` draw at an explicit size with exact price geometry, and return an error for a size that is not positive and finite. `ChartTheme`, `indicators`, and `geometry` move unchanged.
- **Maps.** `maps::Camera`, `LatLng`, `LatLngBounds`, `MapFeature`, `MapStyle`, and `PinCategory` move unchanged, with `features_drawing`, `graticule`, `pin_drawing`, `pin_origin`, `zoom_button_drawing`, and `zoom_steps` for the ink the leptoskit map drew.

Every drawing is an `InkDrawing`: SVG path data with a light and a dark `Tone` per path. `runs()` groups paths by tone for renderers that recolour ink through a text colour, and `to_svg(appearance)` writes a standalone SVG document.

The workspace no longer depends on leptoskit or leptos, so it drops its `[patch.crates-io]` pin of leptoskit `main`. The docs replace the three leptoskit guides with [skribble for Rust](https://openbudgetfun.github.io/skribble/docs/guides/rust) and a short note on moving to `leptoskit_skribble`.
